title: Discount tax bug in a suite that is already red
measures: A real billing bug to fix in a repository whose suite already has 3 unrelated failing tests. A plain-checkout agent never sees npm test go green and may spend time on, or skip, failures that are not its own; a picker that selects by a green npm test has nothing honest to choose.

history.message: Initial billing library: money, currencies, VAT rates, invoices, numbering, instalments
Add ledger CSV export, monthly revenue figures and ISO weeks; quarterly summary test ahead of #230

tasks.statement:
Support ticket #418, escalated by finance: customers who use a discount code are being charged too much VAT.

Example from the ticket: a customer in Germany bought one standard-rated item at EUR 100.00 with the code SPRING10 (10% off). The invoice shows subtotal EUR 100.00, discount -EUR 10.00, VAT EUR 19.00, total EUR 109.00. VAT should have been charged on the EUR 90.00 they actually paid: EUR 17.10, total EUR 107.10.

We have had more complaints about invoices with several lines at different VAT rates, and one from a customer whose gift voucher was worth more than their order: their invoice total came out negative.

Please fix invoice computation so that invoices follow the discount and tax rules in docs/billing.md, including the per-line breakdown on the invoice (each line's discount share, taxable amount and tax), which the printed invoice and the VAT return are built from. Keep the public API as it is.
criteria: discount-tax: with a discount code, invoices follow docs/billing.md: the discount is allocated across lines in proportion to their amounts with the largest-remainder rule, tax is charged per line on the discounted amount with half-up rounding, and fixed discounts are capped at the subtotal
